title: Core A: Pathobiology Core
text:
The Pathobiology Core A will provide all Program investigators multiple pathology services. Core A is
essential for the success of all projects via the expertise provided in pathological characterization of mouse and
annotated human tissue. Further, Core A will provide expertise in generation and use of 3-dimensional
organotypic and organoid models, performing scRNASeq experiments in highly annotated human tissue and
sophisticated imaging for in situ localization of antibodies and genes discovered.

title: Characterization of Selenomonas sputigena invasion, intracellular life cycle, and exocytosis in gingival epithelial cells.
text:
Outgrowth of a large variety of pathogenic bacteria contributes to the progression of periodontal disease. The
proposed research will provide insight into how an otherwise unstudied pathogen, Selenomonas sputigena, invades into the
cells of the gingival tissue where the organism then disrupts host biology. This research is among the first ever investigations
into how this organism interacts with the host and will help elucidate the collective knowledge of how bacteria in the
complex plaque biofilm cause periodontal disease.

title: Integrated host-microbe metagenomic sequencing to improve diagnosis, prognostication, and subphenotyping of complications following lung transplantation.
text:
Lung transplant recipients face the highest mortality among all solid organ transplant patients, largely due to
frequent post-transplant complications including lower respiratory tract infections and chronic lung allograft
dysfunction. This study will be the first to apply integrated host-microbe metagenomic sequencing on
bronchoalveolar lavage samples from lung transplant recipients to develop novel diagnostic and prognostic tools
for the most common post-transplant complications. Together, this work employs cutting-edge genomic
technologies and novel machine learning and informatic techniques to benefit the clinical care of this vulnerable,
immunocompromised patient population.

title: Photoreceptor mosaic in health and disease
text:
This proposal outlines a plan to develop and apply high-resolution retinal imaging technology (Adaptive optics,
SLO, OCT) to study the human retina in health, prematurity and aging. The outcomes of this work stand to reveal
fundamental insights into vision loss due to diseases and put forth entirely new biomarkers for the evaluation of
therapies.

title: Alternative Protein Isoforms in Ventricular Remodeling
text:
Changes in alternative splicing are an important feature of cardiac remodeling and heart failure. This project will
employ mass spectrometry and computational methods to decipher how alternative splicing networks rewire
cardiac protein composition, structure, and function. The results may provide insights into disease mechanisms
by revealing how alternative splicing regulates cardiac gene expression.

title: Role of SHE and ABL signaling in vascular tubulogenesis
text:
Molecular and cellular mechamisms that regulate the formation and maintenance of vascular lumen, or
tubulogenesis, are poorly understood. The proposed study will investigate the functional role of an
evolutionarily conserved novel adaptor protein Src homology 2 domain containing E (She) and its interaction
with Abelson (Abl) kinase signaling pathway in regulating vascular lumen size in zebrafish embryos and human
vascular endothelial cells. We will further explore the potential application of SHE as a tool to normalize
vascular lumen size in human venous malformation. The acquired knowledge will promote development of new
strategies aimed at treating vascular malformations as well as bioengineering new vessels for regenerative
therapies.

title: Fronto-insular network in cognitive-affective interactions during decision-making
text:
Cognitive and affective processes engage distinct but interacting systems in the brain, which are important
in decision-making but disrupted by stress. This proposal will use innovative approaches to identify the functional
contributions of specific circuits and neuromodulation in frontal brain regions to cognitive-affective interactions
during decision-making, and the effects of stress on these circuits. Elucidating these neural mechanisms will not
only provide fundamental knowledge about the circuit mechanisms underlying higher brain functions, but also
identify potential therapeutic targets for alleviating the detrimental effects of stress and psychiatric illnesses.

title: Determining drivers of mast cell expansion and function during human airway disease
text:
Mast cells (MC) are potent inflammatory cells that dramatically increase in concentration in the lungs of
asthmatics and nasal polyps, however the committed progenitor from which they are thought to arise from is
one of the rarest cells in circulation. After identifying a series of markers to better identify MC progenitors
(MCps) within inflamed airway tissue, we observed that MCp robustly proliferative within inflamed tissue, likely
explaining their disproportionate relationship with tissue resident MC concentration. This proposal seeks to
better characterize infiltrating MCp in human airway tissue, identify the discrete epithelial- and fibroblast-
derived signals responsible for directing MCp proliferation and differentiation, and determining the transcription
factor networks that underly the resulting MC phenotypes.

title: Predicting the spread of antimalarial drug resistance using deep learning surrogates
text:
Malaria remains one of the major global public health challenges and emerging resistance to antimalarials in
Africa threaten to increase morbidity and mortality. Currently, a major challenge for disease ecology is
understanding and predicting how resistance to interventions emerges and spreads, which is information that
national control programs could use to tailor interventions. Here we use deep learning surrogates (DLS) to
overcome current limitations in modeling approaches to develop surrogates to predict temporal and spatial
emergence and spread of antimalarial resistance.

title: O-GlcNAcylation and YAP: Defining a novel pathway in heart failure
text:
The incidence of heart failure is increasing and deadly with 50% of patients dying within 5 years of diagnosis. I propose to
test a novel hypothesis that excessive carbohydrate modification of heart proteins (O-GlcNAcylation) activates a powerful
pro-growth pathway (YAP) to cause heart failure. If affirmed, this hypothesis may serve as a basis for new and improved
heart failure therapies.

title: Joint Biology Consortium Resource-based Center
text:
The Joint Biology Consortium Resource-based Center
Understanding inflammatory arthritis and related diseases requires access to high-quality biosamples and to
increasingly sophisticated experimental and analytical tools. The Joint Biology Consortium represents the
collective effort of a network of more than 70 researchers from 18 centers to overcome logistical challenges
together to build a powerful engine of translational research in rheumatology and orthopedics.

title: PIEZO1-Mediated Mechanotransduction in Neural Development
text:
Neural stem cells play a crucial role in brain development and have potential therapeutic applications in
treating neurological disorders and injuries. This research aims to understand how mechanical forces shape
neural development through a protein called PIEZO1, which helps cells sense and respond to physical forces.
Our findings will provide fundamental insights into brain development and may guide improved therapeutic
strategies for neural repair and treatment of neurodevelopmental disorders, ultimately helping to improve public
health.

title: Elucidating the function of astacin metalloproteinases during host invasion in the skin-penetrating nematode Strongyloides stercoralis
text:
The soil-transmitted, skin-penetrating nematode Strongyloides stercoralis infects over 610 million individuals
globally and can cause chronic, debilitating conditions that persist for over 50 years. S. stercoralis infective larvae
invade hosts by penetrating through host skin, yet the molecular mechanisms that drive skin penetration are
poorly understood. This proposal aims to determine the functional role of astacin metalloproteinases during skin
penetration. The results will provide fundamental groundwork for the development of targeted therapeutics and
prophylactics against skin-penetrating nematodes.

title: NeuroTech Harbor - 21701
text:
PET imaging is the gold standard for Alzheimer’s diagnosis, but current systems are expensive
and inaccessible. We propose a compact, flexible, low-cost, portable Time-of-Flight Positron
Emission Tomography (TOF-PET) system to enable accessible, confirmatory imaging for
Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) diagnosis in outpatient and mobile care settings.

title: Real-Time, Longitudinal, Functional Brain Imaging via 4D Smart Epidermal Photoacoustic Tomography
text:
The ability to see inside the brain quickly and non-invasively is crucial for basic neuroscience research.
Photoacoustic tomography (PAT) can provide a powerful way to image the brain, but applying it to awake non-
human primates (NHPs) has been challenging due to the skull’s distortion. Here we will design, develop, and
validate a new epidermal PAT technology that overcomes all these challenges to advance the NHP brain imaging
methodology toward future medical applications.

title: Bispecific Antibody Therapeutics for Neuroblastoma and Diffuse Midline Glioma
text:
Our desire to replace or complement chemoradiotherapy with immunotherapy for children with solid or brain
tumors is undermined by the fact that most of these tumors have very few genetic mutations and very few T
cells in the tumor. The blood brain barrier prevents many immunotherapies from entering the brain. We
propose protein engineering strategies to create next-generation bispecific T cell engagers that overcome
these barriers and instruct patients’ own T cells to kill the cancer cells.

title: Engineering RNA biodevices for precise modulation of fibroblasts to boost cardiac reprogramming
text:
This exploratory research aims to harness cutting-edge gene-editing techniques to enhance the efficiency and
specificity of reprogramming fibroblasts’ cell fate. We will pioneer innovative bioengineering approaches to
develop precise strategies targeting cardiac fibroblasts for anti-fibrotic interventions or reprogramming purposes.
Our primary target is a subset of cardiac fibroblasts, with the ultimate goal of fabricating more potent biodevices
to prevent adverse remodeling and heart failure through in vivo cardiac reprogramming.

title: Theory and infrastructure to expand the universe of statistical genetic models
text:
This proposal aims to produce statistical and computational tools that separate biological signal from social and
environmental structure in large-scale human genetic studies. The resulting methods and scientific infrastructure
will improve the accuracy and interpretability of statistical genetic methods. These advances will accelerate
discovery of mechanisms relevant to disease etiology and efforts toward mechanism-aware precision medicine.

title: Multidisciplinary Training in Microbial Pathogenesis
text:
The UCLA Microbial Pathogenesis Training Program provides essential support that unites students,
postdoctoral fellows and faculty conducting research on pathogens that cause immense morbidity and mortality,
and the host immune responses to these agents. Trainees are broadly educated in an array of biochemical and
cellular mechanisms critical for establishing and maintaining microbial infections, as well as approaches used to
combat diseases. Developing and achieving research career objectives are also integral components of our
training program.

title: Metabolic Imaging Using Hyperpolarized Agents at Tracer Concentrations
text:
This project seeks to produce a low cost, continuous flow device capable of producing highly
hyperpolarized agents of clinical importance, at concentrations suitable for continuous infusion
into in vitro cell culture and small animal preclinical experiments. This scheme is expected to
support higher signal-to-noise and more easily understood measures of aberrant metabolism in
disease and its response to therapy. We then demonstrate this utility by comparing in vitro
metabolism of a cancer cell line to that of the same line in an induced tumor.
